questions.title: Playing shots in a different order to play faster
questions.question: You and your friends play your shots in a different order to help everyone go faster. No one is trying to win by going first. Does anyone get a penalty?

choices.text: No, there is no penalty if you are just playing faster.
Only the first person gets a penalty.

questions.explanation: If you and your friends play out of order only to help play faster, that is okay. No one gets a penalty.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: Something you get if you break a rule, like adding a stroke to your score.
The way players decide who hits their ball first, second, and so on.

questions.teachingTip: Let children know that in friendly games, playing out of order to keep the game moving is okay if everyone agrees and no unfair advantage is taken.
likelyMisconceptions: Children may think you always get a penalty for playing out of order, but you don't if you are just trying to play faster and everyone agrees.

questions.title: Playing out of turn to save time
questions.question: You and your friends decide to play out of turn just to speed up play. If no one is trying to get an advantage, is there a penalty?

choices.text: No penalty as long as it is only to speed up play.
Only the first person gets a penalty.

questions.explanation: When playing out of turn to save time, with no special advantage gained, there is no penalty.
